claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use it as a state backend.
The PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable's value should be the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API, e.g. `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`.
When the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable is unset, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves the PULUMI_API_DOMAIN environment variable's domain.

Using a separate domain for PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN keeps the Terraform-compatible API distinct from the Pulumi API, but it is not required, since PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.

In Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, and in the `terraform login`/`tofu login` commands and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name, the configured PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value should be used wherever the state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com`.
Pulumi documentation includes a state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ describing how Terraform and OpenTofu can use a Pulumi Cloud state backend.
